texts.title_text: Three Hong Kong activists face prison for 1989 Tiananmen vigils
texts.slide_1_text: Three Hong Kong activists received prison sentences ranging from five to seven years under the national security law.
texts.slide_2_text: They organized the annual Tiananmen Square vigil, which commemorated the 1989 crackdown and was previously allowed in Hong Kong.
texts.slide_3_text: The court ruled their demands for an end to one-party rule violated the Chinese constitution.
texts.slide_4_text: France and Germany condemned the sentences, calling peaceful human rights advocacy a fundamental right.
